## The problem

Comparing courses of action with a stochastic combat model is only useful if the comparison is statistically honest (paired, interval-bounded, selection-bias-aware), the discretization is checked, and the parameters have a defined path from notional to calibrated.

## Approach

An entity engine runs on OSM or DEM or synthetic ground: detection hazard, multinomial-logit target choice, circular-normal hit probability, suppression, and Beta breakpoints. It uses named random substreams so COAs share random numbers. Around it sit Wilson/delta/sup-t intervals, Kaplan-Meier and Aalen-Johansen for censored outcomes, Kim-Nelson ranking-and-selection, a Latin hypercube design with a stochastic-kriging GP and Saltelli/Jansen Sobol indices, and history matching (implausibility, NROY waves) with a held-out terrain coverage check. An aggregate brigade engine is derived as a mean-field limit of the entity kill chain and bias-corrected against it.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why it matters for a decision

Supports COA analysis (which Blue scheme of maneuver is best, with what confidence) and shows the V&V and calibration process that Army analytic organizations apply to combat models. The outputs are methodological, not operational, because every parameter is notional.
:::

## Results

| Result | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Paired comparison with common random numbers: support-by-fire 0.678 [0.658, 0.699] vs maneuver 0.649 [0.628, 0.670], n=2000 each; paired difference +0.029 [+0.009, +0.050]; CRN halved the variance | scripts/headline.py -> runs/headline.json + manifest |
| Grid cell size is not converged: the 25 m vs 12.5 m gap is 0.169 at a 7.5 s tick (non-overlapping intervals), larger than the tactical effect the model measures, so absolute probabilities are partly a grid artifact | scripts/convergence.py --reps 1500 -> runs/convergence.json |
| 43 of 47 test suites pass in 10 min 55 s, backing the verified-claims table | pytest tests/test_sim.py test_stats.py test_calibration.py test_brigade.py |
| Sobol sensitivity: probability of kill at tank range dominates (total-order 0.61-0.79), metamodel LOO R2 0.75-0.86 | scripts/doe_sobol.py -> runs/sobol_rung1.json |

Every result above is traced to a script, log, or artifact in the repository. See [How I Check My Work](/approach.qmd).

## Limitations

- Parameters are notional; nothing is fitted to or checked against real data
- Absolute win probabilities are partly a grid artifact; only fixed-cell paired comparisons are defensible
- Brigade table runs at n=20 replications; raising it costs about an hour of CPU

## Tools

Python, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn (GP), pandas, Streamlit, pydeck, Altair, OpenStreetMap / Overpass, AWS Terrain Tiles, pytest
